q: Wie viel Verteidigung gibt der Große Graben?
answer:
Der **Große Graben** gibt laut seiner Karte **10 Verteidigung**, sobald er gebaut ist. Mit den täglichen Weiterentwicklungen kommt mehr dazu (bis Stufe 5) [1]:

- Stufe 1: +20
- Stufe 2: +45
- Stufe 3: +75
- Stufe 4: +110
- Stufe 5: +150

**Nicht geprüft:** Die Werte steigen von Stufe zu Stufe. Wahrscheinlich ist jeder Wert der gesamte Zusatzbonus auf dieser Stufe und wird nicht zu den vorherigen addiert. Auf Stufe 5 wären das etwa 10 + 150 = 160 Verteidigung. Aus der Karte geht das aber nicht eindeutig hervor.

**Gut zu wissen:**
- Bau: 70 AP, keine Ressourcen. Voraussetzung ist die **Verstärkte Stadtmauer** [1].
- Weiterentwicklungen kosten weder AP noch Ressourcen. Die Stadt stimmt einmal pro Tag ab, und meist wird nur eine Weiterentwicklung pro Tag gebaut [2].
- Der Graben schaltet **Buddelgruben, Fallgruben, Pfahlgraben und Wassergraben** frei [1].

facts.fact: Base defense of 10 points
Daily upgrades raise it, up to 160 defense at level 5

judgement.comment: Base 10 covered; 160 at level 5 stated as probable, hedged but consistent.

q: Combien de PA faut-il pour construire l'Atelier ?
answer:
La construction de l'**Atelier** coûte **25 PA** [1].

Il faut aussi les ressources suivantes : **8× Ferraille** et **10× Planche tordue**. Aucun plan n'est nécessaire, il est disponible dès le début de la partie [1].

Ce que ça apporte :
- L'Atelier est le prérequis de nombreux chantiers avancés : Laboratoire central, Boucherie, Manufacture, Potence, Cantine centrale, etc. [1]
- Ses améliorations quotidiennes réduisent le coût en PA de **tous** les chantiers : −6 %, −12 %, −18 %, puis −25 % au niveau 4 et −35 % au niveau 5. Les niveaux 4 et 5 augmentent aussi le rendement des réparations de +1 puis +2 points [1].

Le Technicien peut aussi utiliser ses Points de Chantier (PC) pour construire les chantiers. Il doit cependant lui rester au moins 1 PA pour pouvoir s'en servir [2].

facts.fact: 25 AP
Also needs 8 wrought iron and 10 twisted planks

judgement.comment: The answer gives 25 PA and the same materials (Ferraille = wrought iron, Planche tordue = twisted plank). The extra details do not conflict with the reference facts.

q: What can I get by opening a toolbox?
answer:
Opening a Toolbox gives you one random item from this list [1]:
- Medicine, 25%
- Explosives, 19%
- Mechanical parts, 17%
- Duct tape, 13%
- Copper pipe, 13%
- Battery, 12%

These are the odds for each opening. The box is used up when you open it.

How to open it:
- **Non-Technicians:** you need a box-opening tool in your bag, and you can't have the injured-hands status.
- **Technicians:** you can open it with a suitable tool, or with no tool at all by spending 1 CP (construction point).

The Toolbox is heavy. It also gives 5 night watch defense if you carry it on watch [1]. You can dig them up in the desert, where they make up about 1.3% of finds in zones that still have digs left [2].

Note: I translated the internal item names myself. Their English in-game names may be slightly different.

facts.fact: Possible contents: battery, mechanical parts (screws and nuts), duct tape, copper pipe, pharmaceutical products, semtex
Pharmaceuticals are the most likely result (about 25%)

judgement.comment: Contents and the top probability match the facts. The bot's own translated names (Medicine for pharmaceuticals, Explosives for semtex) still map correctly. The extra details are unverified but do not contradict any fact.

q: What does the Manipulator hero skill do?
answer:
The Manipulator skill lets you delete entries from the town register (the town log), up to **twice per game**. To delete a line, click the icon next to it [1].

- **Unlock:** after 3 hero days [1].
- **Type:** it's listed as a "legacy" skill. These are the older-style skills that appear in the skill selection screen with the number of hero days each one needs [1] [2].

People often use it to erase a log line they'd rather others didn't see, for example taking something from the bank. My documents don't say whether the deletion itself is recorded anywhere or whether other citizens can see that a line was removed.

facts.fact: Lets you falsify (make unreadable) entries in the town register
Twice per town

judgement.comment: The answer covers the twice-per-town limit. It says entries are deleted rather than falsified (made unreadable), which is close enough to count the effect as covered, though the wording is slightly off.

q: What does the Tamer job do?
answer:
The Tamer is a **hero job**. Players also call it APPRI or BICHON. You start with a Town Uniform and a **Three-legged Labradoodle**, and you get no digging bonus (+0%) [1].

**What you can do with the dog:**
- **Send to the Bank:** while you're outside, the dog carries everything in your rucksack back to the town bank. It works even when the town gates are closed. The plain dog can't carry a **heavy object**, and nothing gets sent if your rucksack is empty [2].
- **Send to the Chest:** same thing, but the items go to your home chest. Your chest needs enough free space for them [2].
- **Feed:** give the dog a steak and it becomes the **Well fed Labradoodle**. That version has no heavy-object warning, so it can probably carry heavy items, though the cards don't state this outright [3].
- **Protects you:** in town, the well-fed dog can stand guard to protect you [3].
- **Bury you:** outside, it costs 1 AP. The dog buries you as a camping hiding spot. This only works in towns where camping is enabled, and not if you're already hidden or buried [3].

After you use "Protects you" or "Bury you", the dog becomes unavailable for a while (a resting state) [3].

The dog's actions menu also lists groups called "fetch", "steal" and "guard" [4]. My documents don't say what those do.

facts.fact: The Tamer has a dog that can carry the contents of their rucksack back to town from anywhere in the World Beyond, once a day

judgement.comment: The answer covers the dog carrying the rucksack contents back to town from outside, but never mentions the once-a-day limit.

q: Comment devenir chaman ?
answer:
Il y a deux façons d'avoir un chaman, et ça dépend du type de ville.

**1. Le chaman élu (rôle)**
- Il faut d'abord construire le chantier **Source Purificatrice d'Âme**. Une assemblée citoyenne se tient alors : débat puis vote, et le citoyen jugé le plus « qualifié » devient Chaman [1] [2].
- Si le chaman meurt, une nouvelle assemblée a lieu pour en élire un autre [1].
- Il reçoit des actions spéciales qui coûtent des points de charlatanisme (PM), 5 par jour d'après le glossaire des joueurs [1] [3] :
  - préparer une potion (1 PM + une gourde) ;
  - soigner certains états (2 PM) ;
  - faire tomber la pluie (3 PM).

**2. Le métier de Chaman (job héros)**
- C'est un métier héros. On commence avec un Masque Voodoo et on voit la position des âmes des citoyens morts récemment [4].
- Mais ce métier est **désactivé dans les villes par défaut**. C'est donc le système par élection qui s'applique en général [5].

**Selon le type de ville**
- En **petite ville**, le rôle de chaman et tout le mode chaman sont désactivés : il n'y a pas de chaman du tout [5].

À savoir : le chaman voit les âmes sur toute la carte, sans pouvoir distinguer les âmes torturées des autres. Il peut les manipuler sans risque [6].

facts.fact: The shaman role is given by a vote of the citizens

judgement.comment: La réponse indique que le chaman est élu par un vote des citoyens. Les détails supplémentaires ne contredisent pas le fait de référence.

q: Can a ghoul drink water?
answer:
Yes, a ghoul can drink water, but it does nothing good for them:

- **Drinking water wounds a ghoul.** Water items have a separate drink action for ghouls. All it does is use up the item and inflict a wound. Ghouls get none of the normal effects, such as the AP refill [1] [2].
- **Ghouls don't need water.** Turning into a ghoul removes Thirsty and Dehydrated, and a ghoul can never become thirsty or die of dehydration [3] [2].
- **This also covers the Survivalist's Survival Book.** If a ghoul succeeds at its "Water" action, they get a wound instead of a drink [3].
- **Some water containers have no ghoul action at all.** On the Water Cooler Bottles, every drink action is for non-ghouls only [4] [5].

Ghouls get AP and reduce their hunger by devouring other citizens instead. Eating a living citizen sets their AP to max +1 (if that's higher than their current AP) and lowers hunger by 65. Eating a corpse left in a house lowers hunger by 10 [6].

In short: only drink as a ghoul if you actually want a wound.

facts.fact: A ghoul can drink a water ration but it inflicts a wound
The ghoul gets none of the normal benefits (no AP restored)

judgement.comment: Both facts covered. The answer also adds extra details that the reference does not check (water cooler bottles, devour numbers), and none of them contradict the facts.

q: Que se passe-t-il si je suis infecté ?
answer:
Être infecté(e) (« Infecté(e) ») a ces effets :

- **Risque de mort au réveil** : d'après la description du statut, si vous ne faites rien, vous avez **une chance sur deux de mourir** au prochain réveil [1].
- **Le statut reste la nuit** : il ne disparaît pas tout seul au changement de jour [1].
- **Veille de nuit** : si vous veillez en étant infecté(e), votre défense baisse de 15 et votre risque de mourir pendant la veille augmente de 10 % [1].
- **Comment s'en débarrasser** : le moyen le plus efficace est de prendre des drogues adaptées [1].
- **Se protéger avant** : l'état « Immunisé(e) », obtenu avec un médicament ou un produit similaire, bloque l'infection normale jusqu'à juste après l'attaque [2]. Mais l'immunité **n'empêche pas une blessure de s'infecter** : pansez vos blessures [3].
- **Goules** : elles ne peuvent pas être infectées, et elles perdent toute infection au changement de jour [3].

facts.fact: An infection can kill you during the night: 50% chance of death (75% in hardcore/Pandemonium towns)
It can be treated by taking the right drugs (medicine)

judgement.comment: The 50% chance of death is covered, but the 75% figure for hardcore/Pandemonium towns is not mentioned. The treatment with drugs is covered. No fact is contradicted.

q: What happens if I don't drink for a day?
answer:
If you skip water for one day, you wake up **Thirsty**. Skip a second day and you wake up **Dehydrated**. If you are still Dehydrated when the next night is processed, you die before the zombie attack [1].

**Example:** no water on day 5 means Thirsty on day 6. No water on day 6 means Dehydrated on day 7. Still Dehydrated at the end of day 7 means death that night.

**Other effects:**
- Walking also makes you thirsty. Every 11th move in the desert since your last drink (or since midnight) raises your thirst by one stage. If you are already Dehydrated, that move kills you [1].
- On night watch, Thirsty gives −5 defence. Dehydrated gives −10 and adds some risk of dying [1].
- If you die of thirst, that day doesn't count as fully survived, so it gives no soul points [2].

**How to recover:**
- **Thirsty:** one water removes the status. If it's your first drink of the day, it also brings your AP back to max [3].
- **Dehydrated:** the first water only takes you back to Thirsty and gives no AP. You need a second one to get your AP back and keep your thirst from rising that night [1].
- Hydratone 100mg also cures thirst the same way, but it gives no AP and makes you drugged (addict if you're already drugged).

**Exceptions:** Ghouls never get thirsty. The Cheat Death hero skill stops thirst from rising for one night [1].

facts.fact: You become thirsty, and if you still do not drink you become dehydrated
Dehydration is deadly if not treated

judgement.comment: Both facts are covered: the answer states the Thirsty → Dehydrated progression and that dehydration leads to death. The extra details can't be checked against the reference facts and don't contradict them.

q: What is the difference between small towns and normal towns?
answer:
Small towns compared with normal towns (Distant Regions):

- **Ranking:** small towns are easier, so they don't count for the season ranking. Only Distant Regions and Pandemonium are ranked [1] [2].
- **Map:** the World Beyond is smaller, about 13×13 on average (between 12 and 14) [1] [3].
- **Buildings:** some constructions are already unlocked when the town starts [3].
- **Shaman:** small towns have no shaman role. Other roles stay, for example the catapult operator [3] [4].
- **Pictos:** in most towns, the pictos you earn stay "pending" until the town reaches day 5. In a small town, players with 100 or more soul points have to reach day 8 instead. Guide and night watch pictos are always kept in small towns, on top of the usual five (RP, sandball, ban, theft, soul collector) [5].
- **Soul points:** these documents say nothing about small towns changing the formula. A life of d days gives d×(d+1)/2 points, so 10 days give 55 [5].

The full list of rule values that are different has its own "Town rules" document for small towns, which I didn't open here [1].

facts.fact: Small towns have no shaman role
Night mode is disabled in small towns
Small towns have no explorable ruin
Small towns do not count for the season ranking

judgement.comment: Covers shaman and ranking; misses night mode and ruin. No contradictions.

q: What do I get when I dismantle a broken electrical appliance in the workshop?
answer:
When you **dismantle** a **Broken Electronic Device** (BED) in the Workshop, you get **one random item** [1]:

- Electronic component: 23%
- Handful of nuts and bolts: 18%
- Battery Launcher 1-ITF (empty): 16%
- Battery: 15%
- Radius Radar Beacon: 14%
- Compact detonator: 14%

**Choosing the result:** the technician workbench lets you pick which of these 6 items you get [1].

**AP cost** [2]:
- Normal dismantling: 3 AP. Having a saw or the Factory construction lowers it by 1 each, down to 1 AP with both.
- Technician workbench: 6 AP for a Technician (4 with saw and Factory). Other jobs pay 8 AP (6 with both).
- Technicians spend their construction points first, then AP.
- If you have the "tired" status (0 AP), you can't use the workshop.

The device is taken from the bank and the result goes back to the bank. It must not be broken or poisoned [2].

facts.fact: Possible results: battery, empty battery launcher, electronic component, mechanical parts (screws and nuts), radius radar beacon, detonator
Electronic component is the most likely (about 23%)

judgement.comment: Every result and the 23% figure match. Extra details about AP costs are not verified but do not conflict with the facts.

q: What is the Scavenger's digging bonus?
answer:
The Scavenger gets **+20% dig chance**. It's added to the base chance of 60%, so a normal dig on a zone that isn't depleted starts at 80% instead of 60% [1] [2]. All other jobs get 0 [3].

Other things that change the chance:
- **At night:** −10%. This drops to −2.5% if a Torch or a lit Bedside Lamp is on the zone floor. Public lights remove it for citizens who have their effect [3].
- **Statuses:** "camper" (after a night spent camping) gives +10%, an eye injury halves the chance, and being drunk gives −20%. These don't apply on depleted zones [4].
- **Scouted zones:** +2.5% per zone scout level, up to 3 levels [3].
- **The same bonus helps elsewhere:** it also applies when searching explorable ruins and buildings [2].

Other Scavenger perks:
- Digs every 1h30 instead of every 2h [3].
- Sees roughly how many digs a zone has left [3].
- Gets 7min30 of ruin exploration time instead of 5min [2].
- Can use the Small Spade's "Excavate zone" once a day to regenerate an empty zone [2].

facts.fact: +20% chance to find something when digging

judgement.comment: States +20% dig chance clearly; the extra details are not checked against the reference facts but do not contradict them.

q: What is the chance to find something when digging in a depleted zone?
answer:
On a depleted zone the base chance to find something is **35%**, compared with 60% on a zone that still has digs [1].

What changes it:
- **Night (19:00–06:59):** −10%. It drops to −2.5% if an item that removes the night penalty, such as a lit Bedside Lamp, is on the zone floor. The Novelty Lamps construction can remove it completely [2].
- **Scout level of the zone:** +2.5% per level, up to +7.5% at level 3. This bonus still applies on depleted zones [1].
- **No effect when depleted:** the job dig bonus, the camper bonus (+10%), the eye wound (which halves the chance) and being drunk (−20%) only count on zones that still have digs [2].
- **Final limits:** the result is always kept between 10% and 90% [3].

That gives about 35% by day, 25% at night (32.5% with a lamp), and up to 42.5% by day on a zone at scout level 3.

When you do find something on a depleted zone, it comes from a separate "empty zone" loot table, not the normal one [3].

I took these numbers from the summaries and didn't check them against the game code.

facts.fact: 35% base chance in a depleted zone
60% base chance in a non-depleted zone

judgement.comment: Both facts are covered. The extra details can't be checked against the reference facts, and none of them contradicts one.

q: Quelle est la probabilité de mourir en veille ?
answer:
La base est de **8 %**. Ce taux monte selon le nombre de veilles que vous avez déjà faites, puis divers bonus et malus s'appliquent [1].

**Fatigue (ajoutée aux 8 %) selon le nombre de veilles précédentes :**
- Cas normal : 0 / +1 / +4 / +9 / +20 / +30 / +42 / +56 / +72 / +90 %
- Veilleur « pro » : 0 / +1 / +4 / +9 / +15 / +20 / +30 / +40 / +50 / +60 / +75 / +90 %. Le code ne dit pas qui a ce bonus. Ce serait probablement le petit bonus du Gardien [2], mais je ne l'ai pas vérifié.

**Ce qui baisse le risque :**
- Les objets portés qui ont une valeur de défense en veille. Certains se cumulent par exemplaire, les autres ne comptent qu'une fois.
- Chaque bain à la piscine : −1 %, mais seulement sur la part due à la fatigue (jamais sous 8 %).
- Être une goule : −5 %.
- Le bâtiment de défense des veilleurs : −5 %.
- Le chemin de ronde au niveau 3 : −1 %.

**Ce qui l'augmente :**
- Les arroseurs automatiques : +4 %.
- Certains états, avec un malus propre à chacun.

**Type de ville :** en Pandémonium, le risque final est **doublé**.

**Blessure et terreur :** elles sont calculées à partir de ce risque. Le risque de blessure est plus élevé en Pandé. L'état « bonne odeur » ramène blessure et terreur à 0.

Exemple : en ville normale, sans objet, à votre 5ᵉ veille (4 déjà faites), le risque est de 8 + 20 = **28 %**.

facts.fact: Base death chance of 8% per watch
The chance increases with the number of previous night watches (fatigue)

judgement.comment: Both facts are covered. The extra details cannot be checked against the references, and the uncertain part is flagged as unverified.

q: Does night time change anything when digging?
answer:
Yes. Night digging carries a penalty, but only when night mode is enabled for the town. It's on by default and off in small towns.

- **When it's night:** from 19:00 to 06:59. What counts is the time the dig actually happens, not when you check the result [1].
- **Penalty:** −10% to your dig chance in the desert. Searching a building gets the same −10% [2].
- **Lowering it:** if an item that blocks the night effect lies on the zone floor, such as a lit Bedside Lamp, the penalty drops to a quarter (−2.5%). Novelty Lamps can remove it completely [3].
- **Ruins you explore inside:** no night penalty at all [2].
- **Final roll:** after the penalty, the dig chance is still held between 10% and 90%, so a night dig never drops below 10% [1].
- **Small towns:** night mode is off there, so digging has no night penalty. Scout spotting still loses 5 at night even in small towns [4].

Example: a Resident searching the Nuclear Bunker has 90% by day and 80% at night [3].

facts.fact: Yes, digging success is lower at night
A torch or lamp reduces the night penalty

judgement.comment: Both facts are covered: the answer says night lowers dig success and that a lamp reduces the penalty. It adds details, but none conflict with the reference.

q: ca sert a quoi le gros trou autour de la ville
answer:
C'est le **Grand fossé** (souvent appelé « GF ») : un grand trou creusé tout autour de la ville, qui sert de défense contre la Horde [1].

- **Coût** : 70 PA et **aucune ressource**. Il faut d'abord avoir construit la Muraille.
- **Défense** : seulement 10 au départ, mais il peut être amélioré dans les améliorations du jour, jusqu'au niveau 5 : 30 → 55 → 85 → 120 → 160 points de défense. C'est donc un bon investissement sur le long terme.
- **Débloque** d'autres chantiers : Galeries des Fouineurs, Oubliettes, Fosse à pieux et Douves. C'est le « remplir avec un tas de choses » dont parle sa description [1].

Pour rappel, chaque point de défense de la ville bloque 1 zombie pendant l'attaque. Par contre, si la Grande Porte est ouverte, aucune défense ne compte, fossé compris [2].

q: how many AP for the first wall
answer:
The first wall is the **Defensive Wall** (FR: Muraille). It costs **25 AP** and gives **30 defence** [1].

- **Resources:** 4× Wrought Iron + 8× Twisted Plank. The card lists a variant at the same 25 AP with 5× Wrought Iron + 10× Twisted Plank, marked as both the Pandemonium version and the easy version [1].

q: est-ce qu'il est vrai que les éclaireurs peuvent renforcer les fouilles
answer:
**Oui, mais indirectement.** L'Éclaireur lui-même ne fouille pas mieux : son bonus de fouille est de **+0 %** [1].

En revanche, c'est le seul métier qui laisse des « marques de passage » sur les zones qu'il visite. Chaque niveau d'éclairage d'une zone ajoute **+2,5 points** de chance de fouille, jusqu'à **+7,5 points** au maximum [2] [3] [4]. Ce bonus vaut pour **tous les citoyens** qui fouillent la zone ensuite, pas seulement pour l'éclaireur.

Pour situer ce bonus, par fouille [3] :
- Zone qui a encore des objets : 60 % de chance de base pour un Habitant, 80 % pour un Fouineur.
- Zone épuisée : 35 %.
- La nuit : −10 points (réduit à −2,5 points avec un objet lumineux posé au sol de la zone).
- Campeur averti : +10 points. Blessure à l'œil : chance divisée par 2. Ivresse : −20 points.

Le bonus d'éclairage est ajouté en dernier, après tous ces modificateurs [4]. Une zone bien éclairée donne donc un petit coup de pouce, mais rien de comparable à un Fouineur.

q: quel est le meilleur spot de camping ?
answer:
En général, c'est l'**Abri anti-atomique** : il donne le plus gros bonus de camping (+50) et accueille jusqu'à 5 campeurs. On le trouve entre 10 et 13 km de la ville [1].

Les suivants :
- **Ancien commissariat** : +30, entre 6 et 9 km, 4 places [2]
- **Tente d'un citoyen** : +30, entre 12 et 15 km, mais 1 seule place [3]
- **Avant-poste militaire** (16 à 19 km, 5 places), **Char d'assaut en panne** et **Bar des illusions perdues** (21 à 28 km) : +20 chacun. Leur distance rapporte en plus +20, ce qui fait environ 40 au total, encore moins que l'Abri [4] [5].

Ce qu'il faut savoir [5] :
- Le bonus du bâtiment ne compte que si tous les décombres ont été déblayés. Sinon, vous n'avez que +15.
- En plein désert, ou si le bâtiment est plein, c'est −25.
- Distance : malus jusqu'à 4 km (de −100 à −10), rien de 5 à 11 km, puis de +5 à +20 à partir de 12 km.
- Chaque zombie dans la case retire 7 (3 seulement avec la tenue de camouflage).
- À partir du 3ᵉ campeur dans la même case, malus de −10 à −70.
- Camper de nuit donne +10. Une tombe donne +8. Chaque objet de camping dans le sac donne +5. Le Phare construit donne +25.
- Les améliorations manuelles (objets, amélioration du campement, tombe) sont plafonnées [6].

Les chances de survie ne dépassent jamais 90 %, sauf pour l'Ermite, qui peut atteindre 100 % [7].

facts.fact: The Nuclear Bunker (Abri anti-atomique, nicknamed AAA) has the highest camping bonus of all ruins: 50

q: is the AAA a good place to camp?
answer:
Yes. The AAA (Nuclear Bunker) is the best ruin for camping in the game.

- **Highest camping bonus:** +50 to your camping chance. The next best ruins give +30 (Old Police Station, Citizen's Tent) and most give +10 [1] [2].
- **5 spots:** up to 5 campers can hide there. Once it's full, the next camper gets −25 instead of +50. Being first matters, because priority goes to whoever hid first [2] [3].
- **Distance:** it spawns 10–13 km from town. At 12–13 km you also get the distance bonus (+5/+7). At 10–11 km there's no bonus or penalty [1] [4].
- **Buried bunker:** the +50 only counts once the ruin is fully cleared of debris. A buried one gives just +15, and only if it still has at least 3 debris. With 1–2 debris left there's no room to hide and you get −25. Clear it completely before camping [2].

Other things still change your chance: −7 per zombie on the zone, penalties if you've camped many times before, −10 to −70 when other people camped there before you, and +10 for hiding at night. Your chance is calculated once, when you hide, and is capped at 90%. Survivalists can reach 100% [3].

As a bonus, the AAA's loot is good: Twinoid, Metal Chests and Radar Beacons [1].

facts.fact: AAA is the Nuclear Bunker (Abri anti-atomique)
It has the highest camping bonus of all ruins (50)

judgement.comment: Both facts are covered. The extra details can't be checked against the reference, but none of them contradicts it.

q: Qu'est-ce qu'un MEK ?
answer:
Un **MEK**, c'est le **Meuble en kit**, un objet encombrant de la catégorie Divers [1] [2].

**À quoi il sert :**
- **À l'atelier**, on le transforme en un meuble au hasard : Vieille porte (20 %), Chaise Ektörp-Gluten (27 %), Tréteau (16 %), Table Järpen (16 %) ou Rocking Chair (21 %). Le **Technicien** peut choisir le meuble qu'il obtient [2].
- On le transforme souvent pour avoir la **Table Järpen**, indispensable pour construire le Registre de chantier et la Manufacture [1].
- **En veille**, il donne **15 de défense**, mais il est détruit pendant la nuit [2].
- Tel quel, il ne rapporte aucun point de décoration [2].

**Où le trouver :**
- Bibliothèque de quartier : 60 % des objets trouvés
- Meubles Kiela : 29 %
- Hôtel abandonné : 0,6 %
- En fouillant le désert : 1,2 % des objets trouvés

[2]
